new.story: A Japanese 100 yen coin dated Heisei 27 (2015). One side is filled with cherry blossoms, the sakura, Japan's beloved unofficial national flower; the other carries a big, plain 100. This design has served on the 100 yen since 1967, across three emperors.
new.notes: Both sides photographed. The value side reads 100 with the era date below it, read character by character from enlarged crops as Heisei 27 (2015). The blossom side carries the state name and the denomination in kanji around the flowers. Japan Mint; no mint letter on the type.
